patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: I jumped off the top of the slide because my friend dared me. I landed on my arm, and now my left elbow is all fat and I can't move it. My fingers feel kind of tingly.
presentation.triageNote: 6-year-old boy after a fall from playground height onto an outstretched arm, with a markedly swollen, tender left elbow held rigidly still and mild finger paresthesias. The distal pulse is currently present and the hand remains warm and pink.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because finger paresthesias accompanying a markedly swollen elbow injury suggest possible neurovascular compromise and make this a high-risk extremity presentation.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This child has a markedly swollen elbow after a fall, with finger paresthesias that may signal threatened nerve or vascular function.
clinical.acuityReason: The combination of major swelling, guarded motion, significant pain, and a distal sensory complaint requires rapid evaluation and serial neurovascular checks.
expectedResources: Immediate and repeated distal neurovascular examinations
Reduction or operative treatment if indicated
keyFindings: Fall from playground height onto an outstretched arm
Markedly swollen and tender left elbow
redFlags: Finger paresthesias after a markedly swollen elbow injury
teachingPoints: Distal pulse alone does not exclude a clinically important nerve or vascular injury.
Sensation, motor function, perfusion, and pulse should be documented repeatedly before and after splinting or reduction.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Rapid imaging and orthopedic assessment would likely lead to reduction and stabilization, with operative fixation if the injury is displaced or neurovascular findings persist.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: sitting, cradling a swollen elbow, holding it very still
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a hispanic 6-year-old boy in playground clothes, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: sitting, cradling a visibly swollen elbow and holding it very still. Expression: in real pain and worried. Clearly visible: a swollen left elbow held rigidly still. No text, no logos.
